doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Quitting in St. Louis; the planted cripple who is cured on stage
summary: He stayed four or five months and quit in St. Louis; he describes the local plant who is miraculously cured by the tonic.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How long did you stay with the show together? Oh God, not, not too long, maybe four or five months. Four or five months? Mm-hmm. And I quit, I quit in St. Louis. That's when I started working with Faith. What else you would start to tell us about, uh, Charlie and him? About what the, what all you did on the show? Uh, he says, you know, the doc would come out first and throw out the, the court. Well, he would, the doc was, uh, more or less, uh, an emcee and a straight man. After you, you did your acts, uh, we, we would, uh, he would usually make a spiel for the medicine, you know, and demonstration. And then, uh, we had, uh, we had our shields, uh, out in the audience. We'd have a cat out there, man, would come up there on crutches, you know, come limping up on the stage, you know, and suppose they've had arthritis and rheumatism and TB for 40 years or something. And then, and he can't walk. And doc says, well, man, he says, sit on here in this chair. And doc, he says, and this cat was shaking like he had the heebie-jeebies, you know, going along. Doc says, now you just be calm. Just be calm, friend. Pat him on the head, you know. And then this cat's shaking. Help me, doc. Man, he's going through an act better than peated lorry could ever go. Help me, doc. He says, I'm dying. Doc says, just be calm, friend.

Now, folks, he says, now, you see this poor fella here? This poor fella is practically dying on his seat. And this doc, help me, doc. Help me. Help me. I'm dying. Now, he says, I will show you. He says, I'll give you a demonstration here. Give this fella a shot of this moon's tonic.

Man and doc are pouring out a glass of little, little shot glass of this moon's tonic. Man, and this cat would stop shaking all at once. Suddenly, huh? Yeah. And he calmed down. Well, not too sudden, you know, gradually. It's according to how good an act he was.
We'd replace these cats. Was this always a guy from that town or did you carry this cat? No, from the town.

We'd pick up somebody. No, doc ain't gonna spend no money to carry no man just for a little short act like that. So, he'd go ahead and pass and set this thing up. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. He said, we hit a guy, you know,

and doc was out and give him this shot and this guy was calm, calm. People would, often the audience would be just compounded. Yeah. Especially when we got a real good actor. He'd get a captain, man, that could win an academy award sometimes. Man, he would calm down and he'd jump up and do a buck in wing. We taught him
